data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The fairness question is genuinely undecidable without empirical simulation: no a priori structural argument can predict whether the specific seed 42 and horizon 10000 produce counts within the tolerance, because the outcome depends on the precise interaction of the starting point with the orbit structure of the LCG modulo 6.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If a closed-form or analytical argument can predict the counts within the tolerance without running the full recurrence, the undecidability claim is refuted.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the simulation reveals a pattern that could have been predicted from the multiplier's properties mod 6 and the seed, the claim of undecidability is weakened.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The LCG has period 2^31 and visits every state in {0, ..., 2^31-1} exactly once before repeating. The mod 6 projection induces a sequence of residues. While the aggregate distribution over the full period is determined by the divisibility of 2^31 by 6, any finite subsequence's distribution depends on where in the orbit it starts. Seed 42 determines a specific entry point, and the first 10000 terms may or may not sample the residues evenly. There is no closed-form shortcut to determine the counts without running the recurrence (as stated in the problem). Therefore, the only responsible epistemic stance is to withhold judgment until the simulation produces the actual counts. The simulation proposal filed here will adjudicate.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
